title: Rehydrate GraphQL resolver trace context and replay async spans for exporter ordering
creator: Jordan Kim
description: GraphQL resolvers in several services spawn detached async work (background jobs, resumable flows) that currently lose trace context or emit spans with out-of-order timestamps when they reach Tempo/Jaeger via our OTLP pipeline. This makes trace timelines confusing for customers and reduces the value of latency/error dashboards. This ticket implements: 1) rehydration of trace context at resolver boundaries for safe propagation into async workers, and 2) a delayed-span replay buffer on the exporter path that reorders and coalesces short-lived async spans to maintain temporal appearance and parent-child relationships when exporting to Tempo/Jaeger.
technical_design: High level: (1) Instrumentation layer change: extend the GraphQL middleware to snap and persist a lightweight context blob (traceid, spanid, sampled bit, baggage) into the tenant-scoped async task envelope. Provide a small helper in our telemetry SDK for worker rehydration that re-creates the active span as a child of the original resolver span. (2) Exporter-side replay buffer: add a bounded in-memory buffer in the OTLP/HTTP exporter where asynchronous spans with 'replay_candidate=true' are held for up to 250ms to allow arrival of their parent/related spans; buffer performs stable sort by event timestamp and collapses transient child spans into a single aggregated span if they are sub-5ms and share the same parent to reduce noise. (3) Backpressure and safety: the buffer has circuit-breaker thresholds (max_count_per_tenant, max_total_bytes). When limits exceed, it falls back to passing spans through with a 'replay_skipped' attribute and signals metrics. (4) Export compatibility: ensure re-serialized spans maintain OTLP v0.17 field layout and that Tempo ingestion ordering hints (timestamp, parent_span_id) are preserved. (5) Feature flag and rollout: implement feature flag per-org and per-service to enable rehydration and replay independently for testing.
tasks: Add GraphQL middleware helper to capture and serialize trace context into task envelopes
Add SDK helper to rehydrate context and start child span in async workers
Implement exporter-side replay buffer with configurable window and aggregation rules
Add feature flags and config surfaced in Console for per-tenant toggles
E2E tests: unit + integration against local Tempo/Jaeger dev instances
Create migration/rollback plan and update docs for instrumentation guidance
Perf and chaos tests for buffer backpressure and high-throughput scenarios
acceptance_criteria: GraphQL middleware persists trace context and async worker can rehydrate and produce spans with correct parent-child relationships
Replay buffer reorders async spans correctly in >=95% of synthetic traces with 250ms window
When buffer limits are hit, fallback path emits replay_skipped attribute and metrics increment
No regression in export throughput beyond 5% for standard workloads in load test
Feature flags allow enabling only replay buffer or only rehydration independently
Instrumented e2e demo shows improved trace timelines in Tempo UI for a GraphQL->async worker flow
rollout_plan: Start with internal beta on staging tenant and two low-traffic services. Enable rehydration-only first for developer services to validate parenting. Then enable exporter replay buffer behind feature flag for same tenants and run synthetic trace generator for 48 hours. Monitor replay_metrics and tempo_ingest_errors on dashboards. If replay_dropped_by_tenant > 0.1% or export error rate increases by >0.5%, rollback exporter buffer for that tenant. After 1 week of stable metrics, enable gradually for production tenants using percent-based rollout via Console toggles.
qa_plan: Unit tests for serializer/deserializer of trace context; integration tests using local OTLP collector and Tempo; synthetic workload that creates resolver+100ms delayed async child spans; validate ordering and parent ids in Tempo queries. Run load test at 2x baseline throughput to exercise buffer circuit-breaker.
